questions.question: The main advantage of real-time PCR over conventional PCR is that it:

answers.b: Detects amplified DNA only at the end
answers.c: Requires less time for sample preparation

explanations.b: Conventional PCR detects the product at the end of the reaction.
explanations.c: Sample preparation time is similar for both techniques.
explanations.d: Conventional PCR uses agarose gel electrophoresis; qPCR uses optical detection instead.

questions.question: If amplification occurs in the NTC after 35 cycles, the most appropriate conclusion is:

explanations.a: NTC contains no template, so amplification should not occur at all.
explanations.b: High efficiency does not explain amplification in a negative control.
explanations.d: Optical readings are functioning, indicating it is a biochemical issue, not a machine failure.

questions.question: The Ct value in real-time PCR represents the following:

answers.b: The cycle at which fluorescence crosses the threshold

explanations.a: Total cycles is the programmed duration (e.g. 40 cycles), not Ct.
explanations.b: The cycle at which fluorescence crosses the threshold.
explanations.c: Ct is independent of the direct amount of primers used.
explanations.d: Ct relates to the initial template concentration, not the plateau concentration.

explanations.a: Lower Ct means the signal was detected earlier, indicating more starting template.
explanations.b: Early crossing indicates highly successful and rapid amplification.
explanations.d: Inhibition would delay amplification, resulting in a higher Ct value.

questions.question: Reverse transcription is required in real-time PCR when the virus contains

explanations.a: DNA can be directly amplified by DNA polymerase.
explanations.b: Single-stranded DNA can be directly converted by DNA polymerase during the first cycle.
explanations.c: Proteins are not target templates for PCR.

questions.question: Which enzyme is used to convert viral RNA into cDNA?

explanations.b: RNA polymerase transcribes DNA into RNA.
explanations.d: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences.

questions.question: The standard curve in qPCR is used to:

answers.c: Calculate viral quantity in unknown samples

explanations.a: Negative controls are used to detect contamination.
explanations.b: Melting curve analysis is used to identify primer specificity.
explanations.c: Calculate viral quantity in unknown samples.
explanations.d: A standard curve does not affect the physical fluorescence output of the reactions.

questions.question: During which PCR step does primer binding occur?

explanations.b: Extension is the elongation phase where DNA polymerase synthesizes DNA.
explanations.c: Primer binding occurs specifically during the annealing step at a regulated temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common application of viral quantification by real-time PCR?

explanations.a: Chromatography is used for protein purification.
explanations.c: Electron microscopy is used for observing viruses physically.
explanations.d: Vaccine preparation involves inactivation or attenuating strains, not molecular qPCR quantification itself.

questions.question: Fluorescence intensity during real-time PCR is directly proportional to:

explanations.a: Intensity changes cyclically but specifically reflects product concentration.
explanations.b: Primers are in excess and their raw amount does not determine transient fluorescence intensity.
explanations.d: Tube size has no effect on fluorescence quantum yield.
